name: Genetic 46,XX Difference of Sex Development

criteria.description: Presence of 46,XX karyotype confirmed by chromosomal analysis
Clinical evidence of ambiguous or atypical external genitalia at birth
Abnormal steroid hormone profile indicating androgen excess or enzyme deficiency
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes involved in sex development (e.g., CYP21A2, CYP11B1, HSD17B3)
Pelvic ultrasound or MRI showing presence of internal female reproductive structures with atypical gonadal morphology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of 46,XX karyotype plus ambiguous genitalia and abnormal hormonal assay consistent with androgen excess or enzyme deficiency
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and imaging support diagnosis and subtype classification.

pathognomonic.notes: Includes clitoromegaly, labioscrotal fusion, and hypospadias-like features
Genetic confirmation of female karyotype despite atypical genitalia
searchTerms: female chromosomes with male physical traits
discordant sex characteristics despite XX karyotype
mismatch between genetic sex and appearance

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of androgen excess or steroidogenic enzyme defects

common.notes: Enlarged clitoris due to androgen exposure
Partial or complete fusion resembling scrotum
Excessive terminal hair growth in androgen-sensitive areas

common.symptomName: Salt-wasting crisis (in congenital adrenal hyperplasia subtype)
common.notes: Life-threatening electrolyte imbalance in some enzyme deficiencies

searchTerms: urethra opening on underside of penis

occasional.notes: Fatigue, hypotension in some enzyme deficiencies

occasional.symptomName: Psychosocial distress related to gender ambiguity
searchTerms: emotional problems due to ambiguous genitalia

rare.notes: Observed in specific enzyme defect subtype
searchTerms: high blood pressure from enzyme deficiency
blood pressure raised by 11-beta hydroxylase problem

rare.notes: Benign adrenal tumors in chronic adrenal hyperplasia

imaging: Pelvic ultrasound showing normal uterus and ovaries
MRI of pelvis for gonadal structure assessment
genetic: Pathogenic variants in CYP21A2, CYP11B1, HSD17B3, or other sex development genes
other: Family history of congenital adrenal hyperplasia or DSD

distinguishingFeatures: Female external genitalia with absent or rudimentary Müllerian structures
Normal or elevated androgen levels with androgen receptor resistance
Different genetic mutations affecting testicular development

redFlags: Severe electrolyte imbalance or salt-wasting crisis in neonate
Ambiguous genitalia at birth requiring urgent evaluation
Rapid virilization in infancy or childhood
references: Hughes IA, et al. Consensus statement on management of intersex disorders. Arch Dis Child. 2006.
Lee PA, et al. Global DSD update since 2006. Horm Res Paediatr. 2016.
